title: 127. Divine Mercy - Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father!

reels.title: God is calling you to a feast, and you have things to do
reels.hook: What is your excuse to God?
reels.why: A well-known parable transposed into modern life with excuses everyone recognizes. It ends with a clear and sharp point about the plow and looking back.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: whoever puts their hand to the plow to plow and then starts looking back at their old life, is not fit for spreading the kingdom of God.

cards.text: What is your excuse to God?
Vladimir Grebenar — dr. sc., Ora et Labora
Interpretation of the parable of the great banquet from the Gospel of Luke (Lk 14:15-24).
“I don't have time, I have things to do…”
Whoever puts their hand to the plow and then starts looking back at their old life, is not fit for spreading the kingdom of God.
Divine Mercy – Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father!

reels.title: Europe is silent, Africa is converting
reels.hook: Europe is silent, and Africa says yes
reels.why: A short and provocative comparison between Europe and Africa. It immediately connects the parable to the state of the Church today.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: Europe won't, there is there is Africa that will.

cards.text: Europe is silent, and Africa says yes
Vladimir Grebenar — dr. sc., Ora et Labora
In the parable of the great banquet, the first invited guests refuse the invitation, so the master calls others.
From paganism to Christianity
Europe won't, there is Africa that will.
Divine Mercy – Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father!

reels.title: What awaits good people who have never heard of Christ?
reels.hook: What about good people who do not know about Christ?
reels.why: It answers a question that many ask. It has an unexpected detail about a priest whom the souls of Muslims visit in a dream.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: God is just and I firmly believe… that Jesus will be proclaimed to them before the final judgment.

cards.text: What about good people who do not know about Christ?
Vladimir Grebenar — dr. sc., Ora et Labora
He speaks of people of other religions to whom no one has proclaimed Christ.
God is just and I firmly believe… that Jesus will be proclaimed to them before the final judgment.
“…the souls of Muslims come in a dream for him to hear their confession.”
Divine Mercy – Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father!

reels.title: Why is it called New Age specifically?
reels.hook: Why is it called “new age” specifically?
reels.why: It begins with a direct question and offers an interpretation that surprises. It mentions specific places of apparitions: Garabandal, Akita, and Međugorje.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: There will not be an end of the world, but a new age will arrive.

cards.text: Why is it called “new age” specifically?
Vladimir Grebenar — dr. sc., Ora et Labora
Grebenar describes the New Age as a mixture of Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism.

“There will not be an end of the world, but a new age will arrive.”

Divine Mercy – Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father!

reels.title: There are no other ways of salvation
reels.hook: Is there more than one path to salvation?
reels.why: A short and uncompromising claim starting right from the first sentence. It is rounded off with one clear message of faith.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: The name Jesus Christ alone is the path to salvation, to eternity.

cards.text: Is there more than one path to salvation?
Vladimir Grebenar — dr. sc., Ora et Labora
Interpretation of the Epistle to the Philippians: “Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father.”
The name Jesus Christ alone is the path to salvation, to eternity.
Divine Mercy – Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father!

reels.title: The baptized face a stricter judgment
reels.hook: Baptism does not make judgment easier for you, but harder
reels.why: An unexpected turn: being a Christian means greater, not lesser responsibility. The message is clear and personal.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: we have a greater obligation, a greater responsibility, a somewhat stricter judgment than those who have not received Christianity.

cards.text: Baptism does not make judgment easier for you, but harder
Vladimir Grebenar — dr. sc., Ora et Labora
Conclusion of the interpretation of the parable of the great banquet (Lk 14:15-24).
We have a greater obligation, a greater responsibility, a somewhat stricter judgment than those who have not received Christianity.
Divine Mercy – Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father!

reels.title: Prayer with other religions? First, one condition
reels.hook: Common prayer with other religions? There is a condition
reels.why: Takes a clear and polemical stance on the topical subject of interreligious gatherings. The thought is rounded off with one clear condition.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: And if he refuses a priori to be baptized, we have we have nothing to do with other religions.

cards.text: Common prayer with other religions? There is a condition
Vladimir Grebenar — dr. sc., Ora et Labora
Grebenar speaks about common prayers, fasting, and proclaiming peace with other religions.
And if he refuses a priori to be baptized, we have nothing to do with other religions.
Divine Mercy – Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father!
